User is interested in AI applications in healthcare, especially medical diagnosis, medical imaging, clinical decision support, patient engagement, personalized medicine, and healthcare management (S1.U1–S1.U6). Current focus: rare genetic disorders, AI-powered rare-disease diagnosis, and using machine learning with genomic, medical-literature, patient, lab, and imaging data (S2.U2–S2.U4). They are learning machine learning through a Coursera course and listen to “The Science Hour” podcast about AI-powered medical diagnosis (S2.U3).

User’s views: key rare-disease AI challenges are insufficient data, need for high-quality standardized/annotated data, and interpretability/explainability for clinician trust. They favor data sharing and collaboration among researchers, clinicians, and patients (S2.U5). They believe AI can democratize care via remote/underserved deployment, personalized plans, remote monitoring, and telemedicine, while requiring equity, transparency, fairness, diverse representation, reduced bias, and safeguards against disparities (S2.U6).

User also requested online resources/documentaries about renewable energy (S2.U1).
